text:
alex_support: Hey team — ACME reported a bunch of 429s last night during their end-of-month ingest. They expected monthly credits to refill at 00:00 local, but calls were still getting 429s until ~00:10. Can someone sanity-check? :eyes:

josh_engineer: Do we have tenant id + timezone? Could be a TZ misalign or cache TTL.

alex_support: Tenant: acme-prod-42, timezone = America/Los_Angeles. Customer says their UI showed zero at 23:59 then refill at 00:00, but API kept rejecting for 10m. They hit streaming retry loops and lost jobs.

elena_billing: pulling logs for tenant acme-prod-42 now. On first pass I see refill job fired at 07:00 UTC (00:00 PDT) but cache invalidation events were delayed.

josh_engineer: Can you paste the refill and cache timestamps? Also any 429 response bodies we captured?

alex_support: Got a snippet from the customer's client logs: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 00:02:13 GMT
Body: {"error":"quota_exhausted","retry_after":60}``` They retried and continued to get 429s until ~00:10.

elena_billing: Server-side timeline (UTC): refill job started 2026-03-16T07:00:01Z, core billing ledger updated 2026-03-16T07:00:02Z, cache write attempt 2026-03-16T07:00:02Z. Cache write ack delayed until 2026-03-16T07:08:50Z. That's the suspicious bit.

josh_engineer: That delay (~8.8m) suggests a Redis replication lag or a throttling/backpressure on cache flush. Any infra incidents around that window? eng-infra/monitoring?

alex_support: Customer says they were bursting strong at 23:58-00:03 with many parallel embed calls — maybe flood + long reconnect storms.

quota-bot: Automated alert: cache-backfill-latency spike for shard r-12, duration 00:07:12, peak latency 4.2s.

josh_engineer: OK. Hypothesis: refill writes balance to ledger, but live token checks still reading stale cache due to replication/flush lag, causing API to continue 429 until cache catches up. Two levers: make refill update authoritative in DB and invalidate reads synchronously for affected tenant, or make API check DB fallback when cache shows zero during typical refill window.

elena_billing: For mitigation we can: 1) manually trigger cache invalidation for acme-prod-42 (done) 2) backfill any failed refill attempts (confirmed ledger already has new credits) 3) follow up with infra on r-12 replication.

alex_support: Customer is asking for temporary credits for the 10m outage window — they lost job runs. What do we typically offer?

elena_billing: For production customers we often do a short-term goodwill credit for measurable impact. I'll propose a credit equal to their average token spend during the outage window. Need authorization from billing lead.

josh_engineer: Long-term fix: (a) add DB fallback for quota checks during refill windows, (b) surface a short-lived read-after-write bypass when refill job completes, and (c) add instrumentation to correlate refill -> cache ack latency and trigger automatic fallback. I can PR (a) and (c) this sprint.

alex_support: Repro steps for support doc: 1) Simulate quota exhaustion then schedule refill at tenant TZ midnight. 2) Flood with concurrent requests at refill time. 3) Observe API behavior when cache ack is delayed. 4) Verify manual cache invalidation resolves 429s. Will write up and attach to incident.

customer_acme: Thanks for the quick turnaround, team. We had to restart a couple of workers to bypass the client-side retry storm. Please keep us posted on the credit offer. :pray:

elena_billing: Filing a short internal SR for credit approval and tagging billing-leads. Also opening infra ticket for r-12 replication lag.

josh_engineer: Adding a note: consider smoothing retry behavior client-side (exponential backoff with jitter) to avoid amplification during the refill window. We'll link to a recommended retry pattern in support doc.

alex_support: I'll follow up with a timeline and attach the support repro. Closing loop once credit approved and infra fixes scheduled. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
